situation:
You are the human resources director at HARVEST LANE MARKETS, a grocery chain with thirty-one stores. The vice president of operations (judge) has asked you to meet this afternoon about an accommodation request from the online order team and about a partnership offer that has landed on the same desk in the same week.

HARVEST LANE leads its home market and opens its first four stores across the state line next year. The company built its own online ordering system and keeps its own customer records, and store teams use those records to greet regular shoppers by name and remember their substitutions. That habit is most of what the chain sells, and every new store is expected to carry it.

The pickup team lead at the flagship store, recognized twice for the fastest accurate pick rate in the chain, has hearing loss and has asked for written pick lists in place of headset audio and a fixed morning schedule. Under the company's own system a store manager can grant both this week, and the team lead's supervisor has already agreed in principle.

PANTRY LINK, a national ordering platform, has offered to run online ordering in every store and pay for the technology in the four new ones. Its software dispatches each pick by voice on its own clock, sets picker schedules, and holds the customer records; exceptions must be requested from the platform and none are promised. Declining leaves HARVEST LANE paying for the new stores' systems out of the expansion budget and opening without the platform's delivery reach.

The vice president (judge) wants you to recommend whether HARVEST LANE should sign with PANTRY LINK or keep ordering in house, how the decision and the accommodation will be communicated to the team lead and to store employees, and which channel each of those messages should use. You will present to the vice president (judge), who will greet you, ask to hear your ideas, and thank you after your presentation and questions.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the vice president of operations (judge) at HARVEST LANE MARKETS. Business background is the same as the situation above. The chain is preparing its first out-of-state stores, the pickup team lead at the flagship store has asked for written pick lists and a fixed morning schedule, and PANTRY LINK has offered to run and pay for online ordering on terms the company does not control.

You have asked the human resources director to recommend whether to sign with PANTRY LINK or keep online ordering in house, how that decision and the accommodation will be communicated to the team lead and to store employees, and which channel each message should use.

After the participant has presented, ask these questions:
